page: Amazon Web Services c9g.large is a compute-optimized instance powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors running at 3.3 GHz. Managed through the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the virtual machine provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. System memory is configured at 4.0 GB total, delivering a 1:2 core-to-RAM allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The processor cache architecture contains 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via dedicated AES hardware instructions.

Benchmark measurements show high single-threaded execution capabilities. The c9g.large achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 2306.0, placing in the top 10% of tested systems, accompanied by top-tier single-threaded compression performance with gzip at 36.49 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.21 GB/sec. Conversely, overall multithreaded capacity is restricted by the two-core ceiling, resulting in lower scores in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation. Memory bandwidth reaches 64.7 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 24.76 GB/sec for large block writes.

The hardware configuration provides dedicated compute power per vCPU on modern ARM silicon without hyperthreading contention. Because there is no bundled local storage, persistent disk operations require network-attached block storage over the 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance delivers steady performance for microservices, lightweight web servers, Redis cache instances, edge proxy workloads, and single-threaded background job workers.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.large is a compute-optimized virtual machine based on 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, featuring custom AWS Neoverse-V3 processors clocked at 3.3 GHz. The instance delivers 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 vCPUs, avoiding hyperthreading contention, alongside 4.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per core. It includes 48 MB of L3 cache, hardware AES encryption support, and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not include local disk storage, relying on external network volumes for persistence. In synthetic benchmarks, c9g.large displays top-tier single-threaded performance, ranking in the top 10% for single-core Geekbench at 2306.0 as well as single-threaded compression throughput. Aggregate multi-core output remains limited by the dual-core profile. With dedicated physical cores and consistent execution speed, c9g.large is suited for lightweight web serving, network proxies, Redis caching, and single-threaded batch data transformations.
